title: Invertibility of the canonical set-sheaf slice inverse mate
statement: Let $(D,K)$ and $(C,J)$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $u:D\to C$ continuous with finite-limit-preserving inverse image on set sheaves. Fix $V\in D$ and assume the induced $u_V:D/V\to C/u(V)$ is continuous for the localized topologies [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $L,L_V$ be the chosen left adjoints on sheaves of sets to precomposition $P,P_V$. Let $j_V,j_U$ be sectionwise restriction, where $U=u(V)$. The direct-image comparison $b:Pj_V\cong j_UP_V$ is identity on every section. The inverse mate $j_VL_V\to Lj_U$ of $b$, formed using the chosen sheaf adjunctions, is an isomorphism. Here the inverse mate at A is adjunct to $j_V(\eta_A)$ followed by $b_{L A}$. This is a statement about that specified map, not just existence of some comparison. The localized inverse image also preserves finite limits.

proof.text: Use the sheafified-representable presentation of slices and the Yoneda adjunction to identify the localized inverse image. Restriction corresponds to product with the sheafified representable. The global inverse image preserves that product and therefore gives the canonical restriction comparison.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, middle diagram and final paragraph

proof.text: Under the equivalences between slice sheaves and objects over the sheafified representable, use the induced over-category adjunction. The product comparison is invertible by finite-limit preservation. Its mate has second projection equal to the original section, by naturality of the global unit and the right triangle identity. Consequently its direct-image square is the identity on sections. Uniqueness under the localized adjunction identifies it with sliceSetPullbackMap.

proof.text: For localized finite-limit preservation, transport the localized inverse image across the fibre/extension equivalences by the normalized induced over-category adjunction. The comparison identifies it with Over.post of the global inverse image followed by Over.map of the proved representable isomorphism. Over.post preserves finite limits, Over.map of an isomorphism is an equivalence, and the extension equivalences preserve and reflect finite limits. Apply the explicit composition lemma to combine the finite-limit preservation instances.
